documents.title: @SarahUnsicker on Twitter
documents.summary: My main account, from 2009 to the eve of the 2016 election. The early years are a solo family-law and special-education attorney and new mother thinking out loud: custody rulings, IEP and 504 questions, Parents as Teachers cuts. From late 2015 it becomes a running commentary on the Missouri legislature as I campaigned for House District 91 — gun bills such as SB 656, voter photo ID, SJR 39, abortion restrictions such as HB 1370, early childhood funding, child poverty and ethics reform.

documents.title: @FictionAsLife on Twitter
documents.summary: My writing account, 2014–2016, tied to my blog. Flash fiction, weekly coffee-share posts and essays on parenting and ADHD sit beside real-time reaction to Ferguson after Michael Brown was killed: questions about police conduct, the grand jury and prosecutor, school suspension disparities and what St. Louis needed to hear. I also wrote here as a volunteer CHADD coordinator offering ADHD training for teachers.

documents.title: @ADDSarah on Twitter
documents.summary: A personal account from 2009 to 2014, mostly 2010: daily life as a lawyer and mother with ADHD. Routines and organizing, breastfeeding and attachment-parenting chats, a premature birth, and notes from a practice in divorce, family drug court and education advocacy. Less policy argument than lived experience of the issues I later legislated on — maternal health, ADHD, special education and family court.

documents.title: 2023 session working notes
documents.summary: My Evernote notebook for the 2023 session: the ranked bill list (UCCJEA child-custody jurisdiction, residential school licensing, the Council on Sex Trafficking and public corruption at the top), drafting status for each refiled bill, planning notes for the Statewide Council on Sex Trafficking and Sexual Exploitation of Children, and open questions about the Agape Boarding School investigation.
